what was tested or checked: URL dataset format check (Sahingoz et al. data)
expected: Phishing and legitimate URLs written the same way
actual result: All legitimate URLs start with http(s)://; 58% of legitimate vs 28% of phishing start with www.
issue identified: Model could learn how the lists were collected instead of what phishing looks like (leakage)
corrective action: Scheme and leading www. removed before feature extraction (url_features.normalise_url)

issue identified: Spam would be mislabelled as phishing or legitimate
corrective action: Only Enron ham (label 0) used as legitimate; spam rows dropped; 2 Nazario mailbox-placeholder messages removed

what was tested or checked: Duplicate and near-duplicate check (same first 300 normalised characters)
corrective action: Exact and near-duplicates removed before splitting (data._dedupe)

actual result: Enron text is pre-tokenised lower-case; Nazario is raw text and HTML
issue identified: Formatting alone could separate the classes
corrective action: All text lower-cased; HTML stripped; links/e-mails/phones replaced by tokens; only a-z0-9 kept (preprocess.normalise)
result after change: Applied to training and to live input identically

actual result: gmail.com style domains inside e-mail addresses were extracted as links
corrective action: E-mail addresses removed before bare-domain search

actual result: Link destroyed by the e-mail masking fix (EL05)
issue identified: '@' trick links (a classic phishing method) were missed
corrective action: Explicit links (scheme or www.) are extracted first; then e-mails; then bare domains

actual result: uncommon_tld = 1 (last number treated as a domain ending)
corrective action: Domain ending must be letters only

what was tested or checked: Single-request speed of the random forest

expected: Clear note that text is outside training data
actual result: No note: Arabic letters were silently removed
issue identified: User could trust a text score that is meaningless
corrective action: Note added when >30% of letters are non-Latin

what was tested or checked: URL model: random forest on 21 lexical features
actual result: F1 0.854; recall 0.80; false alarms 5.2%; precision 0.30 at 5% phishing
issue identified: Failed 3 core URL criteria (recall; safety net; false alarms)
corrective action: Investigated (EL11); first results archived in results/history/v0.1.0

what was tested or checked: Website overlap between URL train and test sets
actual result: 66% of test URLs share a website (registered domain) with a training URL
issue identified: Proposal Stage 3 requires preventing source overlap; scores do not show generalisation to new websites
corrective action: URL split changed to a group split by registered domain (no website in two sets)
result after change: Overlap = 0%; RF falls to F1 0.803 on the stricter split

what was tested or checked: Alternative URL model on the grouped split
actual result: Character n-grams (3-5) + lexical features in one logistic regression: F1 0.957 vs 0.803 for RF in an exploratory grouped hold-out
issue identified: Design decision: RF (proposal Table II) under-performs
corrective action: v0.2.0 uses the hybrid logistic regression; RF kept as the comparator
result after change: Final test: F1 0.947; recall 0.919; false alarms 1.5%; precision 0.82 at 5% phishing

what was tested or checked: URL type with input 'not a link' (E04)
actual result: Accepted and scored as a URL
issue identified: Nonsense input gets a risk score
corrective action: URL inputs with spaces and no link are rejected
result after change: E04 PASS (18/18 edge cases pass in v0.2.0)

actual result: Common words such as 'your', 'to', 'with' shown as warning signs
corrective action: Stop-words still count in the score but are not shown as evidence

what was tested or checked: 40 modern messages not in any dataset
expected: Most phishing caught; few false alarms
actual result: 16/20 phishing in high band and 18/20 high or uncertain; 2/20 legitimate flagged (real paypal.com/ae/home scored 100; a genuine bank-statement e-mail scored 87)
issue identified: Brand names in real sites trigger false alarms; scams without links (gift-card request; 'Hi mum' SMS) are missed
corrective action: Not changed (changing the model to fit the challenge set would be tuning on test data); recorded as limitations

what was tested or checked: E-mail scores near perfect (F1 0.993; 0 false alarms)
actual result: Legitimate e-mails come from one company in 2000-2002 and phishing from 2015-2022
issue identified: Model may partly learn 'Enron vs not Enron' rather than phishing
corrective action: Time-split test and challenge set added as independent checks
result after change: Time split: recall 0.95 -> 0.90 (drop 4.6 points); challenge e-mails: 7/8 caught, 1/8 false alarm
